diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\M{W} \in \R^{N \times r}$ have orthonormal columns and $\M{Z} \in \R^{N \times (N - r)}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The matrix $\M\Sigma_\perp\M{V}_\perp\t$ has dimensions $(M-r)\times N$, so it cannot be the matrix $\M{Z}$ required by Lemma thm:tantheta, which needs $\M{Z}\in\R^{N\times(N-r)}$. Moreover, $(\M\Sigma_\perp\M{V}_\perp\t)^\top\M{\Omega}=\M{V}_\perp\M\Sigma_\perp^\top\M{\Omega}$, whereas the term needing control is $\M\Sigma_\perp\M{V}_\perp\t\M{\Omega}$. Thus the lemma is applied to the wrong matrix, and the displayed bound does not follow as written.

failure_location.quote: Use the result from \cref{thm:tantheta} with $\M{Z} =\M\Sigma_\perp\M{V}_\perp\t $  and $\M{W} = \M{V}_r$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the application with the correct matrix, e.g. use $\M{Z}=\M{V}_\perp\M\Sigma_\perp^\top$ (or handle $\M\Sigma_\perp$ separately) and generalize Lemma thm:tantheta to rectangular $\M{Z}$ with the appropriate effective dimension in the logarithmic factor.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem thm:rrf is invalid for rectangular matrices; the subsequent block-structured and Tucker guarantees that rely on thm:rrf inherit the gap.
issues.title: Misapplication of Lemma thm:tantheta in proof of Theorem thm:rrf
issues.why_classification: The defect is a nontrivial proof gap in a central result, but it can be repaired by a contained correction and a straightforward generalization of the lemma, without changing the overall method.

issues.failure_explanation: Solving the displayed inequality for $\varepsilon$ requires $\varepsilon^2/(2+\varepsilon)=\Gamma$. The positive root is $\varepsilon=(\Gamma+\sqrt{\Gamma^2+8\Gamma})/2$, which is asymptotically $\sqrt{2\Gamma}$ for small $\Gamma$, not $2\Gamma$. The claimed value $2\Gamma$ makes the exponent too small, so the probability bound does not follow and the concentration rate is incorrect.

failure_location.quote: Set the upper bound equal to $\delta/4$, solve the quadratic equation for $\varepsilon$,  and choose the positive root to get $\varepsilon = 2 \Gamma$, where $\Gamma$ is defined in the statement of the theorem.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\varepsilon=2\Gamma$ by the positive solution of $\varepsilon^2/(2+\varepsilon)=\Gamma$ (or equivalently $\varepsilon=(\Gamma+\sqrt{\Gamma^2+8\Gamma})/2$) and propagate the resulting $\sqrt{\Gamma}$-type factor through all dependent bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The main concentration lemma and every range-finder, block-structured, and Tucker guarantee that rely on it are invalid as stated; the error term should decay only as $\sqrt{\Gamma}$, not $\Gamma$, which weakens the sample complexity and approximation bounds.
issues.title: Incorrect solution of the quadratic for epsilon in Lemma thm:tantheta
issues.why_classification: The defect is in the central concentration argument; correcting it changes the rate from $O(\Gamma)$ to $O(\sqrt{\Gamma})$ and invalidates the advertised improved guarantees, which is a major mathematical loss.

issues.failure_explanation: In the single-view bound, $\M{Z}=\M{Q}_\perp\M{Q}_\perp^\top\M{M}$ is $m^d\times n^d$, so $\M{Z}^\top\M{\Psi}$ has $n^d$ rows. The matrix Chernoff dimension in Lemma thm:tantheta is the number of rows of $\M{Z}^\top\M{\Psi}$, hence the logarithmic factor should depend on $n^d$, not on $m^d-\ell_r$. The proof also uses $m^d-\ell_l$. This dimension error makes the bound invalid when $n^d$ is large relative to $m^d$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the logarithmic factor $\ln(8(m^d-\ell_r)/\delta)$ by a factor depending on the effective dimension $n^d$ (e.g. $\ln(8 n^d/\delta)$) and update the lower bound on $\ell_l$ accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The analysis of the single-view block-structured algorithm in Theorem thm:added-1 is invalid for rectangular matrices where $n^d$ is large compared to $m^d$; the required sketch size $\ell_l$ may be underestimated.
issues.title: Wrong dimension in the logarithmic factor of Theorem thm:added-1
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local correction of the dimension in a logarithmic factor, but it changes the sample-size condition and can weaken the guarantee for strongly rectangular matrices.
